Who defines Automotive Ethernet?
IEEE 802
Institute of Electrical and Electronics
Engineers
•Maintains and evolves Ethernet since 1980
•Working group 802 - every Ethernet
standard is numbered 802.x
802.1: bridging, VLAN, TSN
802.3: PHY and MAC
•Vendor-specific extensions are usually
handed to IEEE to gain broad adoption
OPEN Alliance SIG
One-Pair EtherNet special interest group
•Consortium of vehicle manufacturers and
suppliers
•Drives Ethernet adoption for in-vehicle use
•Technical committees write specs for
interoperability, EMC and conformance
testing
•Tracks market readiness of components and
test tools

02 | PHYSICAL LAYER
Full duplex on a single pair
02 | PHYSICAL LAYER
Echo cancellation - the principle
Line = V(A) + V(B)
A receives = Line - V(A) = V(B)
B receives = Line - V(B) = V(A)
•Sending: a node adds its own differential
voltage to the pair
•Receiving: it subtracts its own contribution -
the remainder is the partner's data
•The same technique is used in 1000BASE-T
Symbol synchronisation
Adding and subtracting only works if both nodes
know exactly when each symbol starts.
MASTER
•Configured by the
µC's basic software
•Starts the link
•Defines the symbol
clock
•Aligns phase on
receive
SLAVE (default)
•Runs a training phase
first
•Locks its clock to
the master
•Aligns phase on
receive
Design tip: roles are fixed per link in 100BASE-
T1, so the master/slave assignment is part of
the network design (typically the switch port is
master).
Standard Ethernet PHYs: 100BASE-TX and 1000BASE-T
02 | PHYSICAL LAYER
100BASE-TX 100 Mbit/s
Pairs 2 (separate Tx and Rx), 4 of 8

Coding 4B5B + NRZI + MLT-3

auto-negotiation
Rate 4 × 250 Mbit/s = 1000 Mbit/s

Frame format
Uniform structure for every message
Addressing
MAC addresses identify sender and
receivers
Medium access
Rules for when a node may transmit
•All of this lives in the Ethernet controller
(MAC), typically inside the µC
•MAC and PHY exchange bits over the MII
family (MII, RMII, RGMII, SGMII …)
CSMA/CD - classic shared-medium access
Carrier sense Listen - is the medium busy?
Multiple access Medium free → start sending
Collision detect Two senders? Abort the frame
Backoff Wait a random time, then retry
In the car: 100BASE-T1, 100BASE-TX and 1000BASE-T are
full duplex and point-to-point, so collisions do not occur -
CSMA/CD is present but plays no practical role.

Basic vs tagged MAC frame
Basic Dst MAC Src MAC EtherType Data 46 - 1500 B CRC
Tagged Dst MAC Src MAC VLAN tag EtherType Data 42 - 1500 B CRC

•Destination first: unicast, multicast or broadcast - one sender, one or many receivers.
•CRC is computed over all frame fields with the same algorithm on both ends - guarantees integrity of the whole frame.

Network independence
IP abstracts the link layer - the
same packet travels over
Ethernet, WLAN or cellular
unchanged.
Router
Belongs to several networks (one
IP each) and picks the output
port from its routing table.
Loop protection
Each router decrements TTL
(IPv4) / Hop Limit (IPv6); at 0 the
packet is discarded.

UDP in practice: fire-and-forget and fragmentation
ECU A ECU B
Datagram X (src 50100 →
dst 30501)
Datagram Y (src 30502 →

•No acknowledgement, no waiting - minimal delay
•One datagram can go to many receivers via multicast
or broadcast
IP fragmentation of a large datagram
UDP datagram - e.g. 4,000 bytes
Fragment 1
ID 0x1A2B, offset
0
Fragment 2
ID 0x1A2B, offset
1480
Fragment 3
ID 0x1A2B, offset
2960
lost in transit
Receiver cannot reassemble → entire datagram discarded
•Max UDP datagram: 65,535 B (incl. 8 B header)
•Room in one Ethernet frame: 1,500 - 20 B IPv4 header =

05 | TRANSPORT LAYER
TCP connection lifecycle
ECU A (client) ECU B (server)
SYN seq=4200
SYN+ACK seq=9100 ack=4201
ACK seq=4201 ack=9101
ACK + 100 B data seq=4201 ack=9101
ACK + 50 B data seq=9101 ack=4301
ACK seq=4301 ack=9151
FIN+ACK seq=4301 ack=9151
ACK seq=9151 ack=4302
FIN+ACK seq=9151 ack=4302
ACK seq=4302 ack=9152
1 Connect
Three-way handshake
Each side picks a random Initial
Sequence Number (ISN) and
announces its receive window. SYN
consumes one sequence number.
2 Transfer
Data + acknowledgements
seq = position of the first byte sent;
ack = next byte expected. 100 B from
A moves ack from 4201 to 4301.
3 Close
Four-way termination
FIN from A half-closes the link; B can
still send until it sends its own FIN.
05 | TRANSPORT LAYER
How TCP guarantees delivery
Sequence numbers
Number every byte in the stream so the
receiver can restore the original order,
even if segments arrive late.
Acknowledgements
The receiver confirms what arrived with
the ACK flag and the next expected byte
number.
Window (flow control)
Each segment advertises free receive
buffer, so a sender never overruns its
partner.
Retransmission timer
One timer per segment; if no ACK arrives in
time, the segment is sent again. A valid
ACK clears it.
Plus: a 16-bit checksum over header and data detects corruption; the Ethernet CRC already protects each frame on
the link.

Service-oriented (SOME/IP)
Server
Client

Client
(subscribed)

•Partners find each other at run time (Service

•ECUs can be developed independently of each
other
More than a protocol: SOME/IP is middleware that shapes the ECU software design. AUTOSAR provides a dedicated
path (SOME/IP transformer, Socket Adaptor, SD) from the network up to the application.

SRP = Stream Reservation Protocol: MSRP
(streams), MVRP (VLANs), MMRP (MAC

Roles in an AVB/TSN network
Talker

(e.g. camera)
Bridge
AVB-capable

(e.g. display)
Every bridge must be AVB/TSN-capable:
•Handles the special stream multicast MAC addresses
•Forwarding and queuing for time-sensitive streams (credit-based
shaper, 802.1Qav)
•Updates PTP frames with its own residence time
No IP needed: streams never leave the vehicle network, so
AVB/TSN protocols sit directly on Ethernet - less overhead, lower
latency.

gPTP (IEEE 802.1AS)
Generalised Precision Time Protocol - one
grandmaster clock, every node synchronised; the
precondition for a shared presentation time and
low jitter.

08 | VEHICLE DIAGNOSTICS & DOIP
Tester (client) ECU (server)
Request 22 F1 90 (read VIN)
Positive response 62 F1 90 + VIN
Request 2F … (move seat motor)
Negative response 7F 2F 22
Positive response: request executed, data returned (value,
DTC list …)
Negative response: request refused; the NRC says why - e.g.
0x22 conditions not correct, 0x11 service not supported
ODX description (ISO 22901)
Loaded into the tester at start-up and kept
up to date. Defines diagnostic classes and
the services in them - what to ask, how to
decode the answer.
Typical diagnostic services
Read and clear fault memory (DTCs) · read
sensor values · actuator tests such as a
window motor or seat adjustment.
Tester = client, ECU = server
The tester can be an external workshop
device or an on-board tester in the vehicle.
Diagnostic sessions and secure access
Sessions keep access controlled
Default
session 0x01
Always active at start-up; basic read
services
Extended
session 0x03 Extra services such as actuator tests
Programming
session 0x02 Flash download - needs unlocked ECU
Tester Present (0x3E): sent cyclically as a sign of life
- without it the ECU times out and falls back to the
default session.
Which session a service needs is defined in the ODX
diagnostic description.
Unlocking an ECU for flashing or coding
Log in Tester user signs in to the OEM backend
(user ID + password)
Certificate Backend generates a certificate on
request
Install Certificate is loaded into the tester
Authenticate Tester proves its authorisation to the
ECU
Unlocked ECU accepts flash update or new coding
Inside the certificate
Scope of access rights · period of validity · digital
signature proving it is genuine
08 | VEHICLE DIAGNOSTICS & DOIP
Diagnostics over IP (DoIP) - ISO 13400
Why
Much shorter flash and diagnostic cycles in
production and service workshops.
What
A transport protocol: it carries diagnostic
messages. Services stay defined by UDS (or
legacy KWP2000).
Where
Any IP-capable link - Ethernet in the vehicle,
WLAN or cellular for remote use.
Both UDP and TCP are mandatory (port 13400)
UDP Vehicle discovery, status and configuration
TCP
Diagnostic messages on a fixed, reliable
channel - large data segmented
automatically
DoIP generic header - 8 bytes
0 8 16 24 31
Protocol ver. Inverse ver. Payload type
Payload length
Payload (e.g. SA, TA, UDS data)
Payload type
Meaning
0x0001
Vehicle identification request
0x0004
Vehicle announcement / identification
response
0x0005 /
0x0006
Routing activation request / response
0x8001
Diagnostic message (carries UDS)
0x8002 /
0x8003
Diagnostic message ACK / NACK

DoIP gateway: reaching every ECU from one tester
Diagnostic tester
workshop or on-
board
DoIP gateway
edge node
Ethernet
activation
line
CAN
Seat ECU Door ECU Roof ECU Mirror
ECU
•Gateway needs per ECU: a logical address and the bus
request/response IDs
•Only the gateway needs a full DoIP stack
1 Request
•Tester → gateway via DoIP (TCP)
•UDS 0x22 F1 90 - ReadDataByIdentifier (VIN)
•Target logical address 0x1740 (Seat ECU)
2 Mapping
•Gateway ACKs (0x8002) and unpacks UDS
•Sends on CAN with request ID 0x6A0
•Waits for response ID 0x6A8
3 Response
•Seat ECU answers 0x62 F1 90 + VIN
•Gateway wraps it in DoIP, source 0x1740
•Tester matches it to its request

Quick check: match the job to the OSI layer
A Interface to the application software
B Splitting large messages into small packets
C Physical medium for data transmission
D Converting data into the target format
E Data transfer to other networks
F Organising the connection between end systems
G Addressing, error detection and flow control

?6 Presentation

?3 Network
?2 Data link
?1 Physical
Key takeaways
Physical
Single-pair PHYs (100BASE-T1,
1000BASE-T1, 10BASE-T1S) give
full-duplex Ethernet on light,
cheap harnesses.
Data link
Ethernet II frames, MAC
addressing and VLANs separate
domains and prioritise critical
traffic.
IP & transport
IP decouples from the link; UDP
for fast and one-to-many, TCP
for reliable, ordered data.
SOME/IP
Service-oriented middleware:
methods, events and fields,
found at run time via SD.
AVB / TSN
Layer-2 streaming with
guaranteed latency,
synchronised by gPTP.
DoIP
ISO 13400 transport for UDS -
fast flashing, and gateways
reach legacy-bus ECUs.
